item.title: Tesla halves its China down payment to 39,900 yuan on zero-interest Model 3 and Model Y loans
item.description: Until November 30, Chinese buyers can finance a Model 3, Model Y or Model Y L over five years at 0% with half the usual down payment, as Tesla's sales in China keep falling.

item.title: Italy backs EU-wide approval of Tesla FSD after Salvini's call with Musk, putting the 65% vote bar within reach
item.description: Italy's transport minister says Rome supports a swift EU approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. With Germany already on board, Tesla now has a path past the EU's population rule, but only just.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi now runs until 2 a.m., adding trip sharing, Calm Mode, a live rear camera and Grok in Model Y
item.description: Tesla's driverless ride service now operates from 6 a.m. to 2 a.m., 20 hours a day. The update also adds features aimed at night riders, but Tesla has not said which cities get the new hours.

item.title: Inside the Tesla Cybercab: a battery pack ready for cheaper LFP cells, four swappable modules and no paint shop
item.description: Tesla engineers told Munro Live that the Cybercab's pack has spare room for cheaper LFP cells, is split into four replaceable modules, and that the body is coloured without paint. Optimus may soon plug the robotaxis in.

item.title: Tesla owners pick 36 new Supercharger sites in the latest vote, but a win can take years to become a charger
item.description: Tesla named 36 owner-voted Supercharger locations on October 28, from Cannon Beach to Lossiemouth, and opened a new voting round. Here is where they are, how voting works and why winners do not open overnight.

item.title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 in Hayward with no crash, closing the freeway for 10 hours
item.description: A Tesla Semi burst into flames on a Bay Area freeway on Tuesday evening without hitting anything. The driver was unhurt, but the cause is still unknown, just as Semi volume production ramps up.

item.title: Tesla makes its Houston Robotaxi zone 10 times bigger as its Texas fleet passes 1,000 vehicles
item.description: Tesla's driverless Model Y service in Houston now covers about 254 square miles, from the northwest suburbs through downtown, while its registered robotaxi fleet in Texas tops 1,000 cars.

item.title: Latvia becomes the 10th EU country to approve Tesla FSD (Supervised), but the December vote hinges on the big four
item.description: Latvia has recognized the Dutch approval for Tesla Assisted Driving, yet the ten approving countries hold only about 14% of EU residents. Here is why an EU-wide yes in December needs Germany, France, Italy or Spain.

item.title: South Korean police book 80 Tesla owners for illegally unlocking FSD with aftermarket devices
item.description: Seoul police seized 21 plug-in modules used to switch on FSD in Teslas not approved for it. Most Korean Teslas, including every Shanghai-built Model 3 and Model Y, still cannot legally use the feature.

item.title: Japan cuts its EV subsidy by 40% from January 2027: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y buyers lose ¥508,000
item.description: Japan's trade ministry is shrinking its clean-car grants for cars registered from January 1, 2027. A Tesla Model Y or Model 3 drops from ¥1.27 million to ¥762,000, setting up a year-end rush in one of Tesla's fastest-growing markets.

item.title: Tesla stock jumps 5.2% as Barclays upgrades to Overweight with a $450 target, citing a possible SpaceX merger
item.description: Barclays analyst Dan Levy raised Tesla to Overweight and lifted his price target to $450 from $370, calling a SpaceX merger a key part of the bull case. The stock closed Monday at $391.62, but any deal still faces a tough shareholder vote.

item.title: Turo will let US travelers rent Teslas with FSD (Supervised) from October 28, with a free trial for hosts
item.description: Turo is linking to Tesla's systems to verify which rental Teslas have Full Self-Driving (Supervised) active, giving Tesla a new way to put FSD in front of people who have never tried it.

item.title: ISO 25785-1 explained: the first safety standard for humanoid robots, and what it means for Tesla Optimus
item.description: Humanoid robots like Optimus do not fit existing robot safety rules, because they fall over when they lose power. A new ISO standard, still in draft, is meant to fix that.

item.title: Robotaxi vs Cybercab: what is the difference between Tesla's ride service and its driverless car?
item.description: Robotaxi and Cybercab are often used as if they mean the same thing, but they don't. Robotaxi is Tesla's ride-hailing service; the Cybercab is one of the cars that drives in it. Here is the difference, in plain terms.

item.title: Tesla Cybercabs ferry F1 fans to the US Grand Prix as Austin sightings hit a record and 463 are now registered
item.description: Driverless Cybercabs carried race fans to the Circuit of the Americas this weekend. Trackers logged a record 1,250 sightings on qualifying day, and Texas now lists 463 Cybercabs, though Tesla has not said how many rides it gave.

item.title: Tesla Cybercab riders can now see behind the car on a live camera feed, days before Tesla's NHTSA deadline
item.description: Passengers in Austin's Cybercabs can now open the rear and side cameras during a ride, and a dark-screen quiet mode has appeared too. The update lands just ahead of Tesla's October 30 deadline to answer NHTSA's questions on mirrors and rear-view cameras.

item.title: SpaceX filing says any Tesla merger needs Musk's approval, even though he has stepped back from the talks
item.description: SpaceX's third-quarter 10-Q lists three approvals for a combination with Tesla: its special committee, its board and its controlling shareholder, Elon Musk. Here is what that means for Tesla shareholders.

item.title: Does a Tesla Powerwall pay off in the Netherlands once net metering ends in 2027?
item.description: Dutch net metering ends on 1 January 2027, and Tesla now sells both the Powerwall 3 and the three-phase Powerwall 3P in the Netherlands. Here is what changes, what a battery can realistically save and when it makes sense.

item.title: Inside the new Tesla Roadster: rear-wheel drive, a double-cooled 4680 pack, suction fans and SpaceX cold-gas thrusters
item.description: In a detailed walkaround, Tesla engineering chief Lars Moravy explained what sits under the Roadster's skin: two rear motors with over a megawatt, an aluminium-can 4680 battery, Optimus actuators, four suction fans and a 10,000 psi nitrogen system built with SpaceX.

item.title: Tesla's new Model 3 and Model Y in Japan get vehicle-to-load and a CHAdeMO adapter for 14,000 fast chargers
item.description: Tesla Japan has launched updated Model 3 and Model Y cars that can power appliances, plus a CHAdeMO adapter that unlocks about 14,000 extra fast chargers. A discount worth up to ¥264,000 goes to the first 5,000 buyers.

item.title: Tesla Premium Connectivity vs Standard: what you get, what it costs in the US, UK and Europe, and is it worth it
item.description: Standard Connectivity is free for eight years; Premium costs $9.99, £9.99 or €9.99 a month. What each tier includes, how trials and lifetime Premium work, and when paying makes sense.

item.title: Who will succeed Musk as Tesla CEO? What the board and his pay award say about succession
item.description: Tesla has never named a successor, but Musk must deliver a CEO succession framework to earn the last two tranches of his 2025 award. How Tesla's succession process works, and what the filings allow.

item.title: How much does Starlink cost now? US, UK and German prices after the 2026 increase
item.description: Starlink raised most monthly plans by $5 to $10 in 2026 while hardware got cheaper. Current prices for home and Roam plans, the extra fees, and what it means for Tesla owners using a Starlink Mini.

item.title: Tesla Model 3 vs Model Y in 2026: prices, range, space and which one to buy
item.description: The Model Y costs $1,500 to $3,000 more than the equivalent Model 3 but offers far more cargo space. A side-by-side guide to prices in the US and Europe, range, performance and the cheaper Standard versions.

item.title: Musk's Twitter fraud verdict: November 24 claims deadline, the July ruling, and why Tesla shareholders care
item.description: A jury found two of Musk's 2022 tweets misled Twitter investors, and a judge largely upheld the verdict. Where the case stands, who can claim, and its links to Musk's Tesla share sales.

item.title: Tesla stock ends earnings week up 4.9%: a merger-fuelled rally, then a post-results slide
item.description: Tesla shares closed Friday at $372.22, up 4.9% for the week. Three straight gains ahead of the Q3 report and the SpaceX merger committee news were followed by two down days after the earnings call.

item.title: Tesla cancels the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand after seven years of reservations
item.description: Tesla is refunding Cybertruck deposits in Australia and New Zealand and offering a free year of FSD instead. The move suggests a right-hand-drive Cybertruck, including for the UK, is not coming.

item.title: Starlink Mobile passes 22 million users: how VEON and Rogers customers use SpaceX's phone satellites
item.description: SpaceX's direct-to-phone service grew 37% in a quarter, mostly through partner carriers. What VEON's 11 million users and Rogers' expansion show, and what it could mean for connected Teslas.

item.title: Tesla delivery day checklist: what to prepare, what to inspect and what to do if something is wrong
item.description: A practical guide to collecting a new Tesla in the US, UK or Europe: the app steps before the day, an exterior and interior checklist, and how to report problems.

item.title: Musk and the SEC: from 'funding secured' and the 'Twitter sitter' to a $1.5 million Twitter fine
item.description: How Musk's two biggest SEC cases ended, why he is no longer Tesla's chairman, and what the 2026 settlement over his Twitter stake does and does not change for Tesla.
